technical_and_design_decisions: Migrate the modules into the existing Spring Cloud Stream repository structure and conventions rather than creating a separate repository or framework.
Preserve the externally visible module names, configuration properties, message contracts, and documented behavior wherever compatible with the target repository.
Use the target Spring and Spring Cloud Stream versions already established by the s-c-s repository, including its supported Java version and build tooling.
Implement mqtt, null, shell, splunk, tcp, and jdbc as source or sink applications according to their user stories, and implement aggregator and http-client as processor applications.
Adapt XD-specific configuration, lifecycle, metadata, packaging, and deployment conventions to the target repository rather than copying them unchanged.
Use focused unit tests with mocks for external systems and add integration tests for representative messaging and module wiring scenarios.
Use the repository's existing CI, static analysis, formatting, artifact packaging, and documentation conventions.
assumptions: The source code, tests, documentation, and relevant build configuration for all eight XD modules are available and buildable or sufficiently understandable.
The target s-c-s repository, branch, build infrastructure, dependency management, and module templates already exist.

No new broker, database, Splunk instance, TCP service, MQTT broker, HTTP service, or shell environment needs to be provisioned; external dependencies will be mocked or run using lightweight local test infrastructure.
The migration is a compatibility port, not a redesign or addition of substantial new features.
Existing XD behavior and configuration are the acceptance baseline, except where changes are required by the target Spring Cloud Stream APIs.
The effort includes implementation, tests, documentation, local verification, and CI-related fixes, but excludes release management, production deployment, and long-term maintenance.
Work is estimated for one developer and includes normal code review self-correction and integration troubleshooting effort.
The specification does not identify exact framework versions or acceptance test suites; estimates assume moderate API adaptation and no major incompatibility requiring architectural redesign.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the XD implementations, configuration, message contracts, tests, target repository conventions, and migration gaps for all eight modules; define the module-by-module implementation and verification checklist.
Create or configure the target module structure, Gradle or Maven metadata, dependency declarations, package layout, module descriptors, and baseline application wiring in the s-c-s repository.
Adapt common XD abstractions and cross-cutting concerns such as configuration binding, message conversion, error handling, logging, lifecycle management, test utilities, and metadata generation.
Port the MQTT sink implementation, map its properties and message handling to the target APIs, configure the MQTT client integration, and add focused unit and wiring tests.
Port the null sink behavior, preserve accepted input and configuration semantics, integrate it with the target module model, and add unit and wiring tests.
Port shell command execution, input handling, process lifecycle behavior, exit and error handling, configuration mapping, and tests using controlled command execution.
Port Splunk event submission, endpoint and authentication configuration, message formatting, failure handling, target integration, and tests with a mocked Splunk endpoint.
Port TCP connection and message writing behavior, connection lifecycle and retry handling, property mapping, target integration, and socket-based tests.
Port JDBC polling or query-based source behavior, database configuration, row-to-message conversion, scheduling and lifecycle behavior, target integration, and tests using an embedded database.

Adapt aggregation and message-grouping behavior to the target processor model, including correlation, release strategy, persistence or in-memory state assumptions, timeout behavior, configuration, and tests.
Adapt outbound HTTP request processing, request and response mapping, headers, error handling, configuration, target processor wiring, and tests against a mock HTTP service.
Complete unit, contract, configuration, serialization, error-path, and representative integration tests across all eight modules; diagnose and correct failures found during the test pass.
Add or update module usage documentation, configuration property descriptions, examples, input/output contracts, migration notes, and generated metadata required by the target repository.
Integrate all modules with repository build profiles and CI checks, resolve dependency or formatting issues, verify artifact packaging, and address static analysis findings.
Run representative source-to-processor-to-sink pipeline scenarios, validate message flow and configuration compatibility, and perform cross-module troubleshooting.
Perform a final implementation review, remove obsolete XD-specific artifacts, normalize naming and repository conventions, update changelog or release notes as applicable, and make final corrections.
